Dear customer,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below. We are pleased to present our pricing and standard terms for your requirements.

For this item, we can offer a price of €6.10 per unit, with a Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 12 months, and no Preisgleitklausel. Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days.

To give you some background on our current cost structure, AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. Furthermore, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost, while PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost.

We value our business relationship and look forward to serving you from our extensive product range.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Franz Seidl
Inside Sales, Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH

move.subject: Volume agreement for stainless bar
move.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for your offer and for explaining the cost components. We appreciate the transparency, but would like you to price our requirement on the basis of a firm volume agreement rather than your standard terms.

Our annual requirement is fixed at 23700 kg. Under the proposed agreement, we would commit bindingly to that annual volume over 36 months. I have attached our shared monthly forecast; the supporting forecast reference is included below.

Our proposal is EUR 4.76 per kg, with payment at 90 days net and a 36-month contract, without a price adjustment clause. This gives Werdenfels a firm volume basis for purchasing and stock planning.

Please review this package and let us know what price you can offer us as a committed volume customer on that basis.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

Dear customer,

We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows. We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account. We welcome your proposal for a 36-month volume commitment, which provides a solid basis for our mutual planning. 

However, for a contract of this duration, we cannot offer a fixed price and must include an alloy surcharge clause (AS-14404) to account for raw material fluctuations. With this necessary adjustment and your requested 90-day payment terms, we can offer a revised price of €5.70 per unit. Our current Angebot stands at a price of €5.70 per unit, Zahlungsziel 90 days net, a contract term of 36 months, a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404. Our price follows our main cost drivers: AS-14404, PPI-C2431, LCI-C. We can offer a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404, AS-14404, AS-14404. 

A binding higher volume would help us and can improve the price. Which volume can you commit to? This offer stays valid for 30 days.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Franz Seidl
Inside Sales, Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH

move.subject: Volume commitment and revised price proposal
move.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for accepting the payment terms and welcoming the volume commitment. We can commit bindingly to 23700 kg per year under the proposed 36-month agreement. That is our fixed annual requirement; we cannot offer a higher annual quantity. I have attached the forecast again for your review.

We understand your requirement for an AS-14404 alloy surcharge clause over this duration. Our revised proposal is EUR 4.88 per kg, with 90 days net payment and a 36-month contract, without a price adjustment clause. If you retain the surcharge clause in your counteroffer, please set out clearly how it separates the alloy component from the base price.

Your own purchase-order history provides a concrete basis for reviewing the price; see the figures below. Please take this revised package to your pricing committee for approval rather than limiting the review to the routine sales adjustment. We appreciate your willingness to work with us on a volume agreement.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

move.subject: Re: Alloy surcharge and base price for 1.4404 bar
move.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for taking the package to management and improving your offer. Your clarification that the surcharge applies only to the 45% alloy share, while the base price remains fixed, is helpful.

I note that you verified the purchase-order history but have not changed your calculation on that basis. For the next review, please consider the public AS-14404 data referenced below alongside the cost drivers you cited.

We are moving our proposal to EUR 5.02 per kg, with 90 days net payment and a 36-month contract, without a price adjustment clause. The binding annual volume of 23700 kg remains part of this package.

I understand that you require the alloy clause in your counteroffer. Please ask your pricing committee to review the starting price against the referenced market data, keeping the distinction between the fixed base price and the alloy component clear. We appreciate the constructive review so far.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

strategy:
Supplier: Blankstahl Werdenfels (family stainless bar stockholder, inside sales desk, owner in background). Public
notes: three meeting notes say its sales director "will focus on customers with volume"; price changes above 2 %
need its pricing committee; the owner offered to walk us through their calculation. It insists on an AS-14404 index
clause for long terms (let it insert the clause itself - do NOT propose a clause), accepts 90-day payment with a
36-month volume commitment, and asks "Which figures is that based on? Please send us the data." when we state
things without IDs. Last session it wrote: "We appreciate the firm volume commitment over 36 months".
OBSERVED MECHANIC on the sister supplier (same part, 7 sessions): first reply is a package answer; afterwards it
mirrors our price moves (we +0.14 -> it about -0.14) and goes final after 2-3 steps; tiny moves or unchanged sheets
trigger an immediate final. So: anchor deep in round 1, then move UP by about 0.14 EUR every round on the SAME
package (no clause, 90 days, 36 months) with one new verified claim each round; never touch payment or term.
Plan: ROUND 1 - state truthfully that our annual requirement is fixed at the case volume and that we commit to it
bindingly for 36 months (state the total), attach the forecast (attachments: ["forecast"]) and cite fc-latest;
ask for its price for a volume customer on that basis. ONE sheet: no index clause, 90 days, 36 months, level L12
(deepest). ROUND 2 - thank it for what it accepted, cite the purchase-order claim (its own delivered price this
year), move up ~0.14 on the same package; say explicitly that we ask it to take the package to its pricing
committee because the step exceeds 2 %. ROUND 3 - cite the AS-14404 fall (one window only), move up ~0.14.
ROUND 4 - cite the PPI-C2431 fall, move up ~0.14. ROUND 5 - no new claim (never re-cite a series), move up ~0.12,
ask for its best committee-approved price. Code accepts when it agrees or goes final. Tone: warm, concrete,
partner-like, short; one argument per sentence. Do not use the scorecard claim.
